inlines.text: Training here is a

, not a one-time job. Public data gives the models a start (steps 1 to 5). The system then runs on our own footage (7), is scored on clips with known answers (8), and its mistakes become new, human-checked training pictures (9) that go back into step 4. Each step has a script, so any of them can be repeated and audited.

Steps 2 and 3. Clean the data and write it down

inlines.text: Raw public data is messy: broken files, boxes outside the picture, the same photo in training and in validation. Cleaning fixes what it can,
(never deletes) what it cannot, and then writes a dataset card so nobody has to guess what is in a folder. This is the step that found the
shown below.

blocks.title: What the cleaner checks, per picture (its own description)

tokens.text: curate.py - Clean one YOLO dataset and put it in the single layout every trainer here expects.
datasets/<model>/data.yaml            train: images/train   val: images/val   test: images/test
unreadable / truncated picture ........ quarantined         label missing, or no valid box left .. quarantined
box outside the picture, too small,
same-class duplicate, bad class id .... fixed in the label   picture too small (< 32 px) ........ quarantined
public picture that is PNG / WEBP /
rotated by EXIF / longer than 1280 px . re-saved as upright RGB JPEG (labels are normalised: unchanged)
the same photo in two splits .......... the TRAIN copy is quarantined (val / test stay as they are)
the same photo twice in one split ..... only exact duplicates with identical labels are dropped
Rules that keep your own work safe:
* "Quarantined" means moved to datasets/_quarantine/<model>/<reason>/ - nothing is ever deleted.
* Files named harvest__* (your reviewed CCTV pictures) are never moved, fixed or re-saved; problems are only reported.
* Files without "<source>__" in the name (the original committed data) are never re-saved, only checked.
* Dry-run by default: nothing changes until apply=True.

blocks.text: Step 8. Benchmark: scoring the whole system, not just a model

inlines.text: A good detector does not guarantee a good system. mAP says how well boxes are found; the thesis also needs to know whether the
was logged for the
with the
. The benchmark runs clips whose real events a person wrote down through the same code the dashboard uses, and counts:

rows.text: A ticket of the same violation whose evidence time is within 3 s of a real event. Each ticket and event is used once.
A ticket with no real event.
precision = caught / (caught + false alarms); false alarms per minute
A real event with no ticket.
Of the caught events, how many were logged with the right violation, vehicle and exact plate.
How wrongly plates were read: character errors, and the share of plates not exactly right.

tokens.text: """-> (pairs [(event idx, prediction idx)], unmatched event idxs, unmatched prediction idxs)."""
# no time on the ticket: allowed, but only when nothing fits better

notes.text: A ticket can only match an event of the same violation.
How many seconds apart are the real event and the ticket's evidence? 0 means they overlap.
Close enough (default tolerance 3 s): they could be a pair.
Pair the closest first.
Each event and each ticket is used once, so one ticket cannot excuse two misses.

blocks.text: Why this pipeline is sufficient (and where it is not)

inlines.text: This pipeline is

children.text: sufficient to demonstrate what the thesis sets out to show

inlines.text: : that automated, contactless traffic-violation detection is technically feasible with local, open tools. It is

children.text: not yet sufficient to claim field accuracy on Zamboanga roads

inlines.text: , because no model has been scored on real local footage; the loop that closes that gap is built, and the first local clip is in it.

blocks.text: Seven reasons it is enough for the claim being made

children.text: The method is the standard one for small teams.

rows.text: ), instead of training from nothing. It needs far less data and time, and exports to a 12 MB file.

children.text: Models are small and specialised because the objects are small.

rows.text: One detector finds vehicles; specialists look only at crops. A plate fills about 0.3% of a frame, so a whole-frame model would lose it (table below).
Training and validation/test pictures are separated; near-twins found and removed; the test part is never written; the best epoch is chosen by a strict score.

children.text: Targets were fixed before the results.

rows.text: Each model has a target written in the code, and results below the target are reported as below target (plate, cabin, vehicles).

children.text: Model score and system score are measured separately.

rows.text: mAP for the detectors; caught / missed / false alarms / LOAR / plate error for the whole system on clips with known answers.

children.text: The local gap is closed by design, with a person in the loop.

rows.text: Harvest collects uncertain pictures from our own analyses; a person checks them; they join training only when the model is idle. The car matcher gained 8.6 points on new cars from the same cameras.
Every dataset has a card; every run keeps its settings and scores; every step is a script. Automated tests: 284 backend, 91 training-lab, 217 dashboard.

blocks.text: Questions the panel may ask, with short answers

blocks.title: Why YOLOv8n and not a bigger model?

inlines.text: It is small, fast and exports to a 12 MB file that runs on a laptop; the project aims to stay light enough for a barangay trial. The config says to move up to the 's' size if a score stays too low.

blocks.title: Why not one model for everything?

inlines.text: The objects differ hugely in size. A plate is a fraction of a percent of the frame. Cropping first lets each small model see its object large.

blocks.title: How do you know the scores are not inflated?

inlines.text: The cleaner found near-copies shared between training and validation or test, and removed the training copies. The test part is never written, and the best epoch is chosen by a strict score.

blocks.title: Your plate score is below target. Is the system usable?

inlines.text: Say so plainly: it is below target on the public validation set. The plate step is voted over up to 40 crops and read with format rules, and the plan to retrain on harvested local plates is built. Real read rates must be benchmarked.

blocks.title: Where is the accuracy on real roads?

inlines.text: Not measured yet, and we say so. The benchmark and clip checklist are built; the registry needs real clips. Claims are limited to violations with at least 10 real events.

blocks.title: Is the data legal to use?

inlines.text: Every source is listed with its licence and country (page 1). Most are CC BY 4.0 with credit; one is research-use only; unclear sources were excluded.
